$comment: THE single truth table for the LOSSLESS field-retype whitelist (F8A first cut). Read from disk by BOTH sides:
Neither implementation may be changed without the other. PRECISELY (same wording discipline as
permission-match-truth-table.json): changing ONE implementation WITHOUT touching this table turns THAT
SIDE'S OWN run red; changing this table turns the OTHER side red too. Both together are what make a
one-sided drift impossible to land quietly. (Do NOT restate this as 'editing one side reddens the far
SCOPE — rows are claims about the WHITELIST ALGEBRA ONLY: 'may this (source -> target) pair be offered by
the dropdown / accepted by the route as LOSSLESS'. LOSSLESS means exactly one thing: the STORED cell values
stay readable under the new type. Nothing is converted; no record data is touched.
WHERE it is enforced (the PATCH /fields/:fieldId route) and which pairs the route DEFERS to the pre-existing
side-effect guards (link / formula / autoNumber / lookup / rollup / attachment / system-stamp endpoints, which
run type-transition handlers this table knows nothing about) is route behaviour, pinned in the route tests —
not here. `excludedTargetTypes` below is only the dropdown-side mirror of that same set: a target in it is
never offered even if a careless table edit named it.

targetCases.name: plain long text offers text back (F8A: the one direction this cut adds)
long text with rich:false offers text back
long text with no property at all reads as non-rich
RICH long text offers NOTHING (raw HTML would be exposed as bare text)
rich must be the boolean true, not a truthy string (mirrors isRichLongTextProperty)
person offers nothing (object/id array would be sprayed as JSON)
checkbox offers nothing (booleans land as true/false, not yes/no)
date offers nothing (ISO text is a silent downgrade)
duration offers nothing (storage shape not verified)
qrcode offers nothing (storage shape not verified)

pairCases.name: number -> text is lossless (the digits stay readable)
text -> number is NOT lossless ('abc' is unreadable as a number)
plain long text -> text is lossless (F8A)
RICH long text -> text is NOT lossless
long text -> number is NOT lossless
text -> select is NOT lossless (the select write path hard-validates; old values can never be saved again)
a type is never its own lossless target (same type is not a retype at all)
an excluded target is never lossless even from a whitelisted source
an excluded source is not in the table either (the ROUTE defers this pair to the endpoint guards — see the route tests)
